<aside class="blog-tldr not-prose"><div class="blog-tldr__label">TL;DR</div><div class="blog-tldr__body">
- Baseline your episode data
- Integrate the 30-day window
- Align post-acute partners early
- Choose a track with eyes open
</div></aside>

Six steps to **CMS TEAM** readiness:

## Step 1 — Baseline your episode data

Analyze historical performance on the five procedures — cost, readmissions, post-acute utilization. Documentation gaps are common: per Optum Advisory, "analysis of one facility found that two-thirds of episodes had zero HCCs coded, suggesting a major opportunity to improve documentation and coding practices."

## Step 2 — Integrate the full 30-day episode

Consolidate hospital, SNF, home health and outpatient data. Because claims data lags roughly six months, hospitals need near-real-time proxies to intervene while it still matters.

## Step 3 — Build post-acute partnerships

Identify high-performing SNFs and home health agencies. Reducing SNF length of stay and avoiding readmissions — which Milliman puts at "roughly $14,000" each — are the biggest financial levers in the episode.

## Step 4 — Redesign discharge and primary-care referral workflows

TEAM requires referral to primary care. HFMA reporting notes hospitals have found the mandatory PCP referral "more challenging than a lot of people thought," with ambiguity over what counts as a referral, the timeline, and which clinicians qualify.

## Step 5 — Engage physicians

Consider gainsharing/co-management arrangements with surgeons; integrate them into weekly huddles with patient- and population-level performance data.

## Step 6 — Stand up real-time monitoring and quality tracking

Track the CQS measures (Hospital-Wide Readmission, PSI 90, THA/TKA PRO-PM) and simulate financial and clinical outcomes of alternative care pathways.

According to Rainfall Health, hospitals can reach R.A.I.N. Compliant™ status in approximately 10 weeks — a company claim.

## Frequently asked questions

### How long does it take to prepare for CMS TEAM?

Rainfall Health claims hospitals using its platform can reach R.A.I.N. Compliant™ status in approximately 10 weeks — a company-stated timeline, not independently verified. Timelines vary by hospital based on existing data infrastructure.

### What is the first step in preparing for CMS TEAM?

The first step is baselining your episode data: analyzing historical cost, readmissions, and post-acute utilization for the five covered procedures.

### Why do post-acute partnerships matter so much for CMS TEAM?

Post-acute care and readmissions are the biggest financial levers inside a 30-day episode — Milliman estimates each avoided readmission saves roughly $14,000.

### What is CMS TEAM's primary-care referral requirement?

TEAM requires hospitals to refer patients to primary care after a covered procedure, though the definition of a qualifying referral and its timeline has caused confusion for many hospitals.

### When does downside risk start under CMS TEAM?

Downside risk begins in Performance Year 2, calendar year 2027.

### Which quality measures matter most under CMS TEAM?

The Composite Quality Score is built from the Hospital-Wide Readmission (HWR) measure, PSI 90, and the THA/TKA PRO-PM.
